fx-net-exports-chain.alt: A flow chart. The dollar appreciates, so each dollar buys more foreign currency. Two branches: US goods cost more abroad (a 20-dollar shirt costs 16 euros at 0.80 euro per dollar and 18 euros at 0.90), so US exports fall; foreign goods cost less in the US (a 45-euro jacket costs 56.25 dollars at 0.80 euro per dollar and 50 dollars at 0.90), so US imports rise. Both lower net exports, X minus M, so aggregate demand shifts left and real GDP and the price level fall in the short run. Made-up rates.
